subject: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 15:08:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / next steps

Jordan / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of pain points and drivers
- Regulatory requirement for PHI processing to remain inside Acme-controlled VPC (data residency / SOC2 + HITRUST considerations).
- Network egress restrictions: only approved outbound endpoints and strict egress filtering.
- Desire for an air-gapped or limited-egress option for the most sensitive workloads.
- Need predictable latency for real-time summarization in clinician-facing tools (SLO: <200ms p95 for single-turn inference).

Goals discussed
- Pilot private deployment in Acme VPC (Q3 timeline) to validate latency and control flows.
- Demonstrate end-to-end data residency and encryption-in-transit + at-rest with your KMS.
- Define networking checklist and runbook for procurement & ops teams.

Networking / infra constraints we captured
- Acme prefers customer-managed NAT gateways and strict egress allowlists.
- No persistent inbound ports open from internet; all control-plane comms must be via mTLS to Redwoods control plane across approved endpoints.
- Optional air-gap: if required, Redwood can deliver an on-prem/appliance pattern but that will add ~6–8 weeks to timeline for packaging and security reviews.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Vivek (solutions) to share the Redwood private deployment network checklist and a short FAQ for your infra team (by Tue, Jul 7).
2) Acme to share a high-level network diagram & allowed CIDR ranges / egress policy (by Fri, Jul 9) — we can redact specifics for this thread if needed.
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with Acme infra + security, Redwood solutions + engineering to walk the checklist and confirm KMS flow (propose Wed Jul 8 or Thu Jul 9).
4) Redwood to provide an initial deployment estimate and a pilot statement of work (SOW) after the deep dive (within 3 business days).

Attachments: I've attached a short 1-page Redwood private deploy summary and our default VPC requirements doc for your infra team.

If that matches your understanding, reply-all with preferred deep-dive times and we'll lock it in.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and aligns with what we heard internally. A few clarifications from our side:

- The pilot should be limited to non-production PHI datasets initially (we'll mirror a sampling of real records in a VPC-hosted staging environment). Full production cutover would follow validation and compliance sign-off.
- For the air-gap: our security council would likely prefer an air-gapped option for any workloads that touch certain high-sensitivity patient identifiers — please include rough cost and timeline delta in the SOW.

We can share a redacted network diagram; I'll coordinate with Priya to get that to you by end-of-week.

For the technical deep dive, Wed Jul 8 at 11:00am PT works for Priya and me. If that's good for your team, confirm and send a calendar invite and dial-in instructions (or Zoom link).

Appreciate the thorough recap.

—Jordan

Jordan / Priya — great to meet you both (virtually). Per Marissa's notes, here's what I'll bring to the deep dive and a short list of items we need from Acme ahead of the call to make it productive:

What Redwood will present on Wed Jul 8 (11:00am PT)
- Private deployment architecture overview (control plane vs data plane separation).
- Network flow diagram showing required egress endpoints, ports, and optional air-gap patterns.
- KMS integration options (customer-managed key rotation, envelope encryption, HSM notes).
- Pilot SOW outline and quotes (high-level ranges only).

Items we need from Acme before the call
- Redacted network diagram with CIDR ranges / NAT layout (PDF).
- Egress policy constraints (are there approved proxy/GW appliance IPs we must route through?).
- KMS provider & whether Acme requires HSM-backed keys (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, on-prem HSM).
- Expected concurrent sessions and peak qps for pilot (ballpark).

If you can drop the network diagram and the egress policy doc to the HubSpot deal or reply-all with the files, I'll pre-review and annotate the checklist ahead of Wed. I'll also include a short runbook for patching and incident response in the packet.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.
